claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Grain refinement or texture modification will produce a refined grain structure or modified texture in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The refined grain structure or modified texture will improve dislocation mobility.
The refined grain structure or modified texture will enhance strain hardening and uniform deformability under dynamic loading.
Adiabatic shear bands are localized-deformation features relevant to high-strain-rate compression.
Grain refinement or texture modification will reduce adiabatic shear-band formation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 15% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will increase uniform deformation by 20% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will improve localization resistance by 30% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will reduce impact-induced energy release by 25% relative to the baseline.
The prediction applies to adiabatic dynamic deformation at strain rates from 1000 s−1 to 3000 s−1.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the grain-refinement or texture-modification technique.

contradictions.description: The stated numerical baseline is quasi-static, whereas the experiment compares untreated and modified specimens under dynamic deformation. It is therefore unclear whether the percentage changes are relative to the reported quasi-static values or to a matched untreated dynamic control.

The prediction gives improvements of 15%, 20%, 30%, and 25%, but the falsification rule only rejects the hypothesis when at least two properties improve by less than 10%. Results can therefore miss all four stated magnitudes without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
